text: UBS posts $1.2B Q4 net profit (+56% YoY), in line revenues of $12.1B, and announces at least $3B in 2026 share buybacks alongside a higher dividend. CET1 slips to 14.4% as invested assets exceed $7T for the first time. Net new assets slow to $8.5B from $37.5B prior quarter, with $14B outflows from the U.S., even as Europe/Asia inflows offset weakness.

meta.note: Tension between buybacks and looming Swiss capital requirements.

text: Novo Nordisk's Copenhagen shares drop about 17% after management pre-releases 2026 guidance showing sales and operating profit down 5-13% at constant FX. The selloff reflects sharply lower U.S. pricing for Wegovy, rising competition (including compounding pharmacies and Eli Lilly), and loss of exclusivity in several ex-U.S. markets, even as early uptake of the oral Wegovy pill is unusually strong (≈170,000 patients after four weeks).

meta.note: Opposing signals between pill demand strength and core revenue erosion created schema tension.

text: Q4 results and 2026 guidance materially exceed expectations as demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound scales. Revenue reaches $19.29B in Q4 (+43% YoY) with U.S. volumes up ~50% while realized prices fall. 2026 revenue is guided to $80-$83B and EPS to $33.50-$35. Market share in U.S. obesity/diabetes reaches ~60.5% in Q4 despite an anticipated low-to-mid-teens global price decline from the TrumpRx framework.

meta.note: Opposing signals between accelerating volume and structurally lower pricing.

text: ADP reports only 22,000 private jobs added in January, below December's revised 37,000 and consensus forecasts. All net gains come from services—primarily education and health (+74,000)—while professional/business services (-57,000), other services (-13,000), and manufacturing (-8,000) contract. Mid-sized firms add jobs; large firms shed ~18,000. Wage growth for job-stayers remains around 4.5%.

meta.note: Tension between headline stability and sharp cross-sector dispersion.

text: The administration reduces federal law-enforcement deployment in Minnesota by about 700 officers (≈25%), leaving roughly 2,000 agents—mostly concentrated in Minneapolis-St. Paul. Operations shift toward custody transfers from cooperating local jails rather than street arrests, with continued monitoring of county compliance. The drawdown is conditional and framed as "targeted" rather than retreat.

meta.note: Ambiguity between tactical redeployment and political de-escalation.

text: AMD shares fall about 17% after Q4 results, marking the worst session since 2017 despite revenue beating estimates. The company guides Q1 to roughly $9.8B (±$300M), above consensus but below some bullish expectations tied to AI buildouts. Management reports accelerating data-center demand, surging CPU uptake for enterprise AI, and a planned inflection in H2 with the Helios server-scale system.

meta.note: Tension between market repricing and underlying demand strength.

text: BLS reschedules the January Employment Situation release to Feb. 11, five days later than planned, with JOLTS moved to Feb. 6 and January CPI to Feb. 13. Market baselines remain anchored to expectations of roughly +60,000 payrolls and 4.4% unemployment despite the temporary absence of official data.

meta.note: Ambiguity over how much the sequencing change alters trading behavior versus information content.

text: Q4 revenue reaches $113.83B (+~18% YoY) and net income $34.46B (+~30%), beating estimates, yet shares slip after-hours. Google Cloud grows ~48% YoY with a $240B backlog (+55% sequential). Advertising rises to $82.28B, but YouTube misses expectations. Alphabet guides 2026 capex to $175-$185B—more than double 2025—directed mainly to AI compute for DeepMind and cloud capacity.

meta.note: Tension between profitability strength and balance-sheet tilt toward heavy infrastructure spend.
